verified_rule_or_conditional_inference: Microsoft defines GRUUs for user agent, voicemail, location-profile, conference endpoint and server instance. They have gruu parameter and sometimes opaque, not the same as an unqualified user AoR. The source refers to IETF draft syntax; final RFC5627 compatibility needs product/edition review.
Contact: ...;+sip.instance="<urn:uuid:...>" has UUID URN syntax; an epid carried in From/To must be consistent with UUID-derived endpoint identity. An endpoint UUID is NOT the human's SIP URI (AoR).

On every outgoing SIP request, compliant UA MUST place own epid in From. Dialog stores remote epid independently. For a mid-dialog request targeting an identified remote endpoint, it uses the stored remote epid in To.

If inbound request To contains an epid that does not match own endpoint epid, the receiving UA MUST discard it without processing or responding. Blind 404/481 response would violate this specific rule.

Registrar validates +sip.instance UUID-URN and agreement with name-derived epid. Mismatch ⇒ 400 for REGISTER; otherwise add UUID to location service. A valid SIPAE token cannot override invalid endpoint binding identity.

Proxy may index by AoR + sip.instance UUID and MUST validate UUID before use. If request/response epid conflicts, SHOULD return 400. The server's binding lookup, local dialog key, and SIPAE security association index have different identity scopes.

Registrar creates GRUU so it routes to proxy with access to location service; it MUST include URI parameter gruu, and generated opaque encoding is not a client-permitted arbitrary opaque-value generator.

Unknown GRUU on routed in-domain request ⇒ 404. No selected live registration for a known GRUU mid-dialog ⇒ 480 SHOULD. Proxy MUST restrict location records to matching GRUU, then copy/create grid parameter and possibly Route info.

A caller may reach multiple registered endpoints via forked INVITE. A distinct 2xx with a different To tag creates its own confirmed dialog. Each 2xx must be independently ACKed; proxy trying to CANCEL losing branch cannot guarantee loser won't already have produced another 2xx.

Ms-Forking: Active appears only in 1xx, indicating proxy may parallel/serial fork so endpoints can gate early media. It does not guarantee only one winning 2xx or unconditionally cancel all remote dialogs.

CANCEL applies to outstanding INVITE transaction, not any already confirmed dialog. Pending branch generally yields 487 to INVITE and 200 for CANCEL separately. After 2xx crossed CANCEL, UAC still ACKs and can terminate unwanted confirmed dialog via BYE.

RFC6026 introduces Accepted state / Timer M for 2xx processing in SIP INVITE client transaction; it changes older RFC3261 INVITE client transaction behavior. This RFC edition is a potential dependency requiring feature/version audit, not proof classic Skype for Business binary implements it.

SIP proxy routing scripts consider privacy-facing published state, delegate/team/work hours/voicemail for incoming call INVITEs, with specific order and DND policy. Do not assume these audio-call routing rules govern all 1:1 instant-message MESSAGE transactions.
On winning 2xx proxy SHOULD generate branch CANCEL with Reason ms-acceptedby AoR. This metadata describes routing outcome, NOT proof no late 2xx or recipient read receipt.

430 Flow Failed may carry P-Dialog-Recovery-Action whose recognized list includes Registration-Route-Set-Update, Dialog-Route-Set-Update, Wait-For-Session-Update. They are different actions, not interchangeable retry hints.
Dialog recovery is negotiated by Supported: Ms-Dialog-Route-Set-Update; absence of support matters. Ms-Safe-Transfer is a separate extension and shouldn't be collapsed into route recovery.

UA enabling recovery for a particular dialog MUST add Supported tag to all requests on that dialog, and SHOULD periodically send target refresh. INVITE dialog may use RFC4028 session timer, SUBSCRIBE dialog RFC3265 refresh.

Proxy with lost record-route HMAC key may send 481. If recovery option is absent and routing state lost, SHOULD reject with 481. If option tag present, proxy MUST send 430 with explicit recovery action. A generic 481 and actionable 430 are not identical.

Registrar seeing dialog-creating request with GRUU and invalid/absent binding or Routable=FALSE SHOULD send 430 with both Registration-Route-Set-Update and Dialog-Route-Set-Update. This is a registration context problem, not proof remote user blocked the IM.

For 430 Dialog-Route-Set-Update alone, UA MUST run target refresh and on success re-send only the original failed request with updated route set / remote target. If recovery fails MUST report original operation failure.

For Registration-Route-Set-Update action, refresh endpoint REGISTER; on success MUST recover all recovery-enabled dialogs bound to endpoint, SHOULD terminate/recreate recovery-disabled dialogs, and MAY/SHOULD retry original dialog-creating operation as scenario-specific. A full-register retry is NOT the same as retransmitting original MESSAGE.

Wait-For-Session-Update with an existing RFC4028 session timer: recovery refresh timer interval SHOULD be at least negotiated session refresh interval, and its expiry MUST run §3.7.5.3.4 procedure. No fixed global retry 5/10/30 seconds in these clauses.

After repeating same request two or more times and receiving 430 again, UA SHOULD stop retrying and report failure. Endless 430 retry loop is not sourced. Exact request-side counter reset semantics remain U.

REGISTER refresh successful with Presence-State: Register-Action=added|fixed can trigger recovery of dialog route sets, and termination/re-creation for dialogs without recovery support. Align with MS-SIPREGE rev17.1's renewal unexpectedly replaced binding cases.

Actual dialog recovery sends target-refresh request (UPDATE on INVITE-based dialog or SUBSCRIBE on SUBSCRIBE dialog), waits for transaction response, extracts Contact and Record-Route URIs and updates local route set and remote target. It may also recover logically-related conference dialogs.

On incoming mid-dialog target-refresh, endpoint SHOULD update route set + remote target from Contact/Record-Route. If not, later requests can receive 430 even when earlier dialog remains logically established.
SIP MESSAGE MAY be associated with existing dialog but does not initiate a new dialog; user agents MUST support text/plain. Contact MUST NOT appear in MESSAGE request or 2xx response.

MESSAGE 200 OK allows assumption delivered to final destination, but explicitly not read by human. 202 Accepted means accepted by intermediate/store-forward/gateway and NOT evidence final endpoint delivery.

UAS should respond promptly; may return 200 without displaying. 4xx/5xx indicate unsuccessful delivery, but 6xx indicates successful arrival with refusal in this RFC's language; 2xx response MUST NOT include body.
The MS-OCSPROT sample INVITE → 200 → ACK → MESSAGE → 200 is one valid *session-based* IM user journey, not proof every MESSAGE needs a preceding INVITE by base RFC3428.

SIP request/response authentication and canonical cnum/crand/rspauth/snum MIC is separate from transaction/dialog IDs and recipient read/delivery acknowledgment; authenticated 200 does not introduce a new application-level read receipt.

IM media MCU receives and forwards MESSAGE and INFO on separate SIP INVITE sessions established with conference participant. Admission, Focus, roster and conference control belong to MS-CONFBAS/MS-CONFPRO, not to this same MCU MESSAGE forwarding algorithm.
INVITE/200 SDP must signal m=message and a=accept-types for IM media. Client media format capability isn't just presence status or server-wide codec capability.

Dial-in client INVITE Request-URI MUST be IM MCU conference URI, not the contact's personal AoR. Dial-out path comes from Focus addUser and MCU-originated INVITE; distinct roles and call establishment state.

MCU publishes participant endpoint-capabilities in conference roster notifications including supported-im-formats, user-agent and Ms-Sender support. On missing accept-types or certain extension non-support, fallback SHOULD be text/plain.

Microsoft Ms-Sender extension tracks actual human sender when MCU forwards a MESSAGE, as From on forwarded message is conference URI, not originator SIP URI. Client should not pretend From gives participant identity directly.

MCU IM INVITE session established ⇒ client MUST notify higher layer media session established. This is not proof every conference participant can receive selected rich text body or that any later MESSAGE delivered.
Client leaves IM session with SIP BYE. Server-side deleteUser can cause MCU to send BYE to client. These are distinct control operations; not REGISTER Expires=0 or deleting conference globally.

Client sends SIP MESSAGE on established IM MCU INVITE dialog. It SHOULD consult all other participant capabilities; it may send multipart/alternative. When multipart sent, all body parts MUST have Content-Transfer-Encoding: binary, other encodings MUST NOT be used in this source profile.

MCU holds Current message ID per conference, initialized to 1 upon creating conference MCU instance. Message-Id: 1*DIGIT is included in MCU response, forwarded MESSAGE and IMDN, not SIP Call-ID, CSeq or MIME Content-ID.

If sender is only client in MCU session, MCU MUST return 200 OK and there will be no separate delivery notification. A 200 in this special case is not evidence another remote recipient read or even exists.

If other clients connected, MCU SHOULD reply 202 Accepted and later send IMDN. MCU MUST put Message-Id in both 200 and 202 and increment current message ID. It then MUST forward MESSAGE to each other client.

If recipient doesn't support Ms-Sender and incoming content text/plain, MCU SHOULD insert human sender URI into forwarded body; if non-plain body and no Ms-Sender, SHOULD record 415 unsupported media for that recipient.

If recipient supports Ms-Sender, MCU MUST include actual sender URI in forwarded Ms-Sender header. For multipart/alternative sent to recipient that doesn't support multipart, MCU SHOULD select supported part; if none, SHOULD record 415. Supported multipart recipient receives full multipart.
Recipient client receiving forwarded MESSAGE MUST send SIP 200 OK and use Ms-Sender if present to identify human original sender; incoming From is conference-URI. Not a human read receipt.

MCU tracks per-forward transaction response/error/timeout plus ms-diagnostics. Once all outgoing forwarded MESSAGE transactions finished, MCU MUST send IMDN via BENOTIFY with Content-Type: application/ms-imdn+xml.

IMDN has message-id and recipient URI/status error list, plus optional key/value entries (e.g. diagnostics). All failed forwards MUST be in IMDN, successful forwards MAY be included. Zero recipients in IMDN means forwarded successfully to all. Client MUST NOT rely on optional success entries.

200 OK to client's outgoing MESSAGE ⇒ client MUST treat forwarding as success to all MCU participants as per source. 202 ⇒ client MUST take Message-Id from response, with default 0 if missing, and wait for correlated IMDN.

Client MUST maintain sendMessageTimer, default 10 seconds. On 202 it MUST start timer; successful correlated IMDN before timeout stops it. If timer expires, client treats pending IMDN as per-recipient 408. No sourced claim this 10 s equals SIP transaction Timer F.

Correlation key is MCU-assigned Message-Id in 202 and later IMDN; Message-Id fallback zero is prescribed on absent response header, but operation for multiple *simultaneous* 202 messages missing Message-Id remains U. Don't silently use Call-ID or CSeq instead.

MCU stores incoming messages as first 40 seconds conference message history to replay to newly joining clients. After 40s, history clears and new MESSAGE not added. The 40-second timer is server-side and not persistent chatroom retention.
User typing or idle information uses SIP INFO on INVITE/IM media session, not arbitrary application "presence state" publication; MCU forwards body to other clients without interpretation.

MCU MUST reply 202 Accepted to INFO. Forward only to recipient participant endpoints supporting Ms-Sender, adding actual sender URI in Ms-Sender header. Must NOT forward INFO to recipient without that extension.

Client receiving 202 treats INFO accepted by MCU, not final recipient delivery. MCU discards downstream INFO response/timeouts and sends no sender notification. INFO's 202 has a weaker delivery contract than MESSAGE's 202+IMDN.

Source wording inconsistency: section titled “Client Receives an INFO Forwarded by the MCU” says client “MUST send a 200 OK response to the incoming MESSAGE request”, although it is describing an INFO, and companion §3.4.2.5.1 forwards INFO. This is a probable document typo, not authority to silently rewrite normative text; check official errata/revision and RFC3261 transaction method semantics. Sender URI from Ms-Sender is a separate instruction.
